findings.description: This bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so objects (including the seeded vendor roster) are stored without an enforced encryption default. Sensitive report data would be at rest unprotected by a customer-managed or specified KMS key.

No ACL is set and no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, so there is no defence-in-depth control preventing a future public ACL or bucket policy from exposing the report data.
The bucket has no logging block, so access to stored reports is not recorded in the audit_trail bucket, hindering detection and forensic investigation of unauthorised access.
Versioning is disabled while force_destroy is true, so objects can be overwritten or the entire bucket and its contents deleted irrecoverably, enabling destructive tampering with archived reports.
The ledger export bucket defines no server-side encryption configuration, leaving financial ledger data stored without an enforced encryption default.
No logging block is configured for this bucket, so reads and writes of ledger exports are not audited to the audit_trail bucket.

The bucket relies only on a private ACL with no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource, leaving no account- or bucket-level guard against accidental public policy or ACL changes on sensitive ledger data.
Versioning is not enabled while force_destroy is true, so ledger export objects can be silently overwritten or destroyed with no recoverable prior version.

The model artifacts bucket has logging and versioning but no server_side_encryption_configuration, so artifacts are stored without an enforced encryption default and could be tampered with or read if the storage layer is compromised.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is attached, so the private ACL is the only barrier against public exposure of model artifacts.
Operational runbooks, which commonly contain internal hostnames, procedures and occasionally credentials, are stored in a bucket with no server-side encryption configuration.
No logging block is defined, so access to runbook content is not recorded for audit or intrusion detection.
The bucket has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, leaving no enforced guard against a future public ACL or policy exposing internal operational documentation.

findings.issue_category: no public access block on log bucket
findings.description: The audit log destination bucket has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block; because it uses the log-delivery-write ACL, an accidental public policy or ACL change would expose access logs for all other buckets.
force_destroy is true on the audit log bucket, allowing Terraform to delete all accumulated access logs and any evidence of prior activity, undermining the integrity of the audit trail.

A vendor roster spreadsheet (likely containing third-party contact and contract data) is uploaded from the repository into a bucket with no default encryption and no kms_key_id or server_side_encryption argument on the object itself, meaning the data is committed to source control and stored unencrypted.
